stem: A 33-year-old patient has repeated vomiting. Testing shows a blood pH of 7.51 and an elevated bicarbonate concentration. The gastric losses precede the laboratory changes. Which of the following best identifies the primary disturbance in this sequence?

options.text: Metabolic acidosis following intestinal bicarbonate loss
options.explanation: Intestinal bicarbonate loss produces an acidic pattern with lower bicarbonate. This patient instead has gastric losses, elevated pH, and a higher bicarbonate concentration.
options.label: A
options.misconception: Applies intestinal bicarbonate-loss acidosis to gastric losses with elevated pH and bicarbonate.

options.text: Respiratory alkalosis following carbon dioxide loss
options.explanation: A primary fall in carbon dioxide would establish a respiratory process. The history identifies gastric acid loss before the alkalotic pattern, supporting a metabolic origin.
options.label: B
options.misconception: Assumes a primary respiratory origin despite gastric acid loss preceding the alkalotic findings.

options.text: Respiratory acidosis following carbon dioxide retention
options.explanation: Carbon dioxide retention shifts the blood toward acidosis. It cannot explain the primary high-pH, high-bicarbonate disturbance following loss of gastric hydrochloric acid.
options.label: C
options.misconception: Uses carbon dioxide retention and respiratory acidosis to explain a primary high-pH disturbance.

options.text: Metabolic acidosis following increased gastric acid stores
options.explanation: The patient is losing gastric acid rather than accumulating it. The measured pH is alkaline, which also contradicts the proposed primary metabolic acidosis.
options.label: D
options.misconception: Assumes gastric acid accumulation and metabolic acidosis despite measured acid loss and an alkaline pH.

options.text: Metabolic alkalosis following gastric acid loss
options.explanation: Vomiting removes gastric hydrochloric acid. The elevated blood pH and bicarbonate concentration fit the resulting primary metabolic alkalosis rather than a primary respiratory disturbance.
options.label: E
options.misconception: No misconception: gastric acid loss followed by elevated pH and bicarbonate supports metabolic alkalosis.

context: Learning objective: Identify the metabolic alkalosis produced by gastric hydrochloric-acid loss. Vomiting removes gastric hydrochloric acid. The elevated blood pH and bicarbonate concentration fit the resulting primary metabolic alkalosis rather than a primary respiratory disturbance.
